source.title: Open problems in the theory of completely positive and copositive matrices

accepted.question_text: For a positive integer n, let CP_n be the cone of real symmetric n x n completely positive matrices, meaning matrices A that can be written as A = B B^T for some entrywise nonnegative matrix B. Is the decision problem that takes a real symmetric n x n matrix A as input and asks whether A is in CP_n an NP-complete problem?

evidence.quote: It is open whether checking membership in CPn is also NP-complete.

accepted.question_text: Let A be a real symmetric entrywise nonnegative n x n matrix, and let G(A) be the graph with vertices 1,...,n and an edge between i and j exactly when i != j and a_ij != 0. Which additional checkable conditions, whether depending on G(A) or not depending on G(A), can be found to determine or certify complete positivity of A, where complete positivity means A = B B^T for some entrywise nonnegative matrix B?

evidence.quote: It would be interesting to obtain additional, graph dependent or not, conditions for complete positivity.

accepted.question_text: For which structurally defined classes of real symmetric matrices can copositivity be fully characterized? Here a real symmetric n x n matrix A is copositive if x^T A x >= 0 for every vector x in the nonnegative orthant R_+^n.

evidence.quote: For what other classes of matrices can copositivity be fully characterized?

accepted.question_text: Characterize the extreme rays of DNN_n, the cone of real symmetric n x n matrices that are both positive semidefinite and entrywise nonnegative. A matrix A in a convex cone K generates an extreme ray when every decomposition A = B + C with B and C in K forces B and C to be scalar multiples of A.
accepted.context_brief: extreme rays of the doubly nonnegative cone

evidence.quote: The extreme rays of the doubly nonnegative cone DN N n are not fully understood.

accepted.question_text: For n > 5, characterize all extreme rays of COP_n, the cone of real symmetric n x n copositive matrices A satisfying x^T A x >= 0 for every vector x in R_+^n. A matrix A in a convex cone K generates an extreme ray when every decomposition A = B + C with B and C in K forces B and C to be scalar multiples of A.

evidence.quote: It is an open question to characterize the extreme rays of COPn for n > 5.

accepted.question_text: Characterize the faces of COP_n and CP_n. Here COP_n is the cone of real symmetric n x n matrices A with x^T A x >= 0 for every x in R_+^n, CP_n is the cone of real symmetric n x n matrices A = B B^T for some entrywise nonnegative B, and a face F of a closed convex cone K is a subset such that every line segment in K with an interior point in F has both endpoints in F.
accepted.context_brief: facial structure of CP and COP cones

evidence.quote: The facial structure of COPn and CPn is not yet fully understood.

accepted.question_text: For general n, is CP_n facially exposed? Here CP_n is the cone of real symmetric n x n matrices A = B B^T for some entrywise nonnegative matrix B. A face F of a closed convex cone K is exposed if there is a nonzero symmetric matrix C such that K is contained in the half-space {X : trace(CX) >= 0} and F = {X in K : trace(CX) = 0}; K is facially exposed if every face is exposed.

evidence.quote: It is unknown whether CPn is facially exposed.

accepted.question_text: For each finite n > 2, compute the maximal angle theta_max(COP_n) and the maximal angle theta_max(PSD_n + N_n), where COP_n is the copositive cone, PSD_n is the cone of real symmetric positive semidefinite n x n matrices, N_n is the cone of real symmetric entrywise nonnegative n x n matrices, and theta_max(K) is the maximum of arccos(trace(XY)) over unit-norm X,Y in the cone K. Are these maximal angles always attained by a pair of matrices P in PSD_n and N in N_n?

evidence.quote: It remains an open question to compute θmax(COPn) as well as θmax(PSDn + Nn) for finite n > 2

accepted.question_text: Given a matrix A in CP_n, determine a completely positive factorization of A, meaning a representation A = B B^T in which B is an entrywise nonnegative matrix.

evidence.quote: The basic open problem is: given A ∈ CPn, determine a cp-factorization of A.

accepted.question_text: For which graph structures G(A) can one systematically determine a completely positive factorization A = B B^T of a completely positive matrix A, where B is entrywise nonnegative and G(A) is the graph with vertices 1,...,n and an edge between i and j exactly when i != j and a_ij != 0?

evidence.quote: Only partial results are known as to finding a factorization of A given that G(A) has a certain structure.

accepted.question_text: If A is an integral matrix in CP_n, meaning a real symmetric n x n matrix with integer entries and A = B B^T for some entrywise nonnegative B, must A have a rational completely positive factorization? Equivalently, must A admit a representation A = sum_i alpha_i b_i b_i^T in which every alpha_i is rational and every vector b_i has rational entries?

evidence.quote: Given a matrix A ∈ CPn all of whose entries are integral, does A always have a rational cp-factorization?

accepted.question_text: Given a completely positive matrix A, determine or estimate its cp-rank cpr(A), defined as the minimum number of columns in an entrywise nonnegative matrix B such that A = B B^T.

evidence.quote: Finding the cp-rank of a given completely positive matrix, or estimating it, is a basic open problem.

accepted.question_text: Determine an exact formula for p_n = max{cpr(A) : A is in CP_n}, where CP_n is the cone of real symmetric n x n matrices A = B B^T with B entrywise nonnegative and cpr(A) is the minimum possible number of columns of such a nonnegative factor B.

evidence.quote: Determining an exact formula for pn is still an open problem

accepted.question_text: Does the Drew-Johnson-Loewy bound hold for n = 6? Equivalently, if p_n = max{cpr(A) : A is in CP_n} and cpr(A) is the minimum number of columns in a nonnegative B with A = B B^T, is p_6 equal to floor(6^2/4) = 9?

evidence.quote: as is the question whether the DJL conjecture holds for n = 6.

accepted.question_text: Characterize the completely positive n x n matrices A for which the Drew-Johnson-Loewy cp-rank bound holds, where the bound is cpr(A) <= floor(n^2/4) and cpr(A) is the minimum number of columns in an entrywise nonnegative B satisfying A = B B^T.

evidence.quote: It is an open problem to characterize those matrices for which the DJL bound holds.

accepted.question_text: Characterize the graphs G for which cpr(G) = tf(G). Here cpr(G) is the maximum cp-rank over all completely positive realizations A of G, a completely positive realization of G is a matrix A in CP_n whose graph G(A) is G, and tf(G) is the maximum number of edges in a triangle-free subgraph of G.
accepted.context_brief: graphs with cpr(G) equal to tf(G)

evidence.quote: It is an open problem to find a complete characterization of those graphs for which cpr(G) = tf(G).

accepted.question_text: Which additional graph families G have the property that every completely positive realization A of G satisfies the Drew-Johnson-Loewy cp-rank bound cpr(A) <= floor(n^2/4), where n is the number of vertices of G and cpr(A) is the minimum number of columns in an entrywise nonnegative B with A = B B^T?

evidence.quote: Are there other graph families for which the DJL bound holds?

accepted.question_text: Which conditions on a completely positive matrix A guarantee cpr(A) = rank(A), where cpr(A) is the minimum number of columns in an entrywise nonnegative B satisfying A = B B^T?

evidence.quote: Which conditions guarantee equality between the cp-rank and the rank?

accepted.question_text: Which algorithms can compute a minimal completely positive factorization of a completely positive matrix A, meaning a factorization A = B B^T with B entrywise nonnegative and with the number of columns of B equal to cpr(A), beyond the few special cases for which such algorithms are already known?

evidence.quote: But only very few algorithms to compute a minimal cp-factorizations were developed so far.

accepted.question_text: Given a real symmetric matrix X that is not in CP_n, construct a copositive matrix Y in COP_n such that trace(XY) < 0. Here CP_n is the cone of real symmetric n x n matrices A = B B^T with B entrywise nonnegative, and COP_n is the cone of real symmetric n x n matrices Y satisfying z^T Y z >= 0 for every z in R_+^n; such a Y gives a cutting plane separating X from CP_n.

evidence.quote: Given X /∈ CPn, construct Y ∈ COPn with hX, Y i < 0.

needs_review.question_text_raw: It would be interesting to find a characterization of complete positivity in terms of comparison tensors.

evidence.quote: It would be interesting to find a characterization of complete positivity in terms of comparison tensors.
